items.headline: A New Lawsuit Claims Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and xAI Illegally Agreed to Slow Down AI
items.summary: A proposed class-action lawsuit filed Friday accuses Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Elon Musk's xAI of striking an illegal agreement to intentionally slow down AI progress. It points to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei publishing an essay calling for the industry to coordinate on "pacing" development, after which the other companies' leaders publicly agreed, which the suit argues amounts to rivals illegally agreeing to hold back how fast their products improve.
items.why_it_matters: There's nothing to act on here, but if you pay for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Grok, it's a useful reality check: a public promise from AI companies to "slow down for safety" can also look, legally, like competitors agreeing to hold back the same product you're paying to keep getting better.

opportunity.angle: Four AI companies just got sued for agreeing to slow down. Wait, isn't slowing down supposed to be the safe move? Here's the twist.

items.headline: DaVinci Resolve Can Now Take Orders From Claude, Right Inside the Editor
items.summary: Blackmagic Design's DaVinci Resolve 21.1 update added a built-in "MCP" connector (a technical bridge that lets an AI assistant talk directly to other software) so Claude, Claude Code, and ChatGPT's Codex can now organize your media, cut highlight reels, and run batch renders inside Resolve using plain-English instructions instead of manual clicking. This AI-assistant control only works in the paid Resolve Studio edition ($295 one-time), not the free version.
items.why_it_matters: This is a legitimate way to hand off tedious, repetitive edits, like syncing multicam clips, sorting a messy media pool, or batch-exporting a render queue, to Claude by just describing what you want, right inside the editor you already use, instead of learning to write scripts yourself.

opportunity.action_note: Update to DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1, go to File > Setup AI Assistants to connect Claude, and test it on a real task this week, like asking it to organize a media pool or batch-rename a render queue.
opportunity.angle: I connected Claude straight to DaVinci Resolve using its new built-in AI bridge. Here's what it can (and can't) actually do for your edit.

items.headline: Threads Adds Podcast Cards, Transcripts, and Guest Tags for Creators
items.summary: Meta's Threads app rolled out new podcast tools: a podcast profile card and banner on a host's profile, episode links that turn into tappable "listen now" cards inside a post, the option to post a full transcript people can read along with, and the ability to tag guests featured in an episode.
items.why_it_matters: If you host a podcast, or turn your livestreams into one, these tools give Threads users an easy way to discover and sample an episode without ever leaving the app, worth testing on your next episode's launch post.

opportunity.action_note: Turn on the podcast profile card on your Threads account and post your next episode there with the transcript attached to see how the new listen-now card performs.
